verdict.line: You lose if you stand still for her E-into-W stun chain; you win if you poke her down at 800 range before she ever gets to use it.

brief.thesis: Urgot's 800-range Q (Corrosive Charge) outranges every tool in Riven's kit — her Q (Broken Wings, 275 range), W (Ki Burst, 260 range), and E (Valor, 250 range) all require her to close distance first. The entire lane is decided by whether she gets her E (Valor) dash off cooldown to close that gap safely; data backs this structurally with a 51.7% Urgot win rate over 632 games and a stated lane and solo-kill advantage for Urgot.

theirWindow.when: her E (Valor) is up and she engages
theirWindow.what: E lets her dash in, block incoming damage, and set up W (Ki Burst) stun at 260 range, which chains into empowered Runic Blade autos and a Q3 knockback. If she lands E clean, back off or use your own E (Disdain) to throw her back out rather than trading blows.

yourWindow.when: her E (Valor) is on cooldown (6-10s by rank)
yourWindow.what: With no gap-close or damage-block available, she cannot safely reach your 800-range Q poke, and your E (Disdain, 475 range) will actually land and hurl her away since she has nothing to dash through it with.

start.why: 52.8% win rate over 650 games as the dominant start (87.3% pick) — the extra sustain and early auto damage matter because every trade you win is one she had to spend her E to start.

boots.why: 50.3% win rate over 527 games (72.7% pick) — Riven's damage is almost entirely physical autos and ability hits, so flat physical reduction blunts her all-in once she does close.

core.why: Shreds the armor she's building against your poke and keeps your Q/W DPS relevant into mid game.
The HP and tenacity-adjacent survivability covers the one window where she does land her E-W stun combo.

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards landing consecutive autos from range during her E (Valor) cooldown windows, shredding her armor before she's close enough to fight back.

summoners.why: 86.6% pick rate at 51.9% win rate — Ignite converts your stated solo-kill advantage into actual kills once your poke and E (Disdain) punish force her into a bad all-in.

playing.title: Take E first at level 1
playing.detail: Skill order opens E (Disdain), giving you an immediate punish for any Q or E engage she tries before level 2.

playing.title: Poke at 800 range, never at her range
playing.detail: Only throw Q (Corrosive Charge) when she can't close in one dash — her Q/W/E all cap out near 250-275 range, so you should never be fighting inside that bubble unprompted.

playing.title: Track her E (Valor) cooldown, not her HP
playing.detail: It's a 10/9/8/7/6s cooldown that gates her entire engage; poke freely the moment it's down and hold position when it's up.

playing.title: Don't eat the full combo
playing.detail: If her W (Ki Burst) stun connects you're locked into empowered Runic Blade autos and a Q3 knockback — use E (Disdain) proactively to throw her out before she gets there, not after.

playing.title: Threaten dives with R from level 6
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death's 2500 range means you can punish any overextension even off-screen; the 100/85/70s cooldown means save it for a real commit, not a poke.

playing.title: Watch her Conqueror stacks in extended trades
playing.detail: Per OP.GG's own read on this matchup, long fights let her stack healing — disengage with Q poke and reset rather than brawling past 4-5 stacks.

playing.title: Rush Steelcaps into Cleaver
playing.detail: Physical reduction first blunts her burst window; Cleaver's armor shred then makes your sustained poke scale through mid game.

brief.patchCaveat: The build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/sample figures above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — range windows, cooldown timing, and trade sequencing — is my own tactical read on top of that data.
